newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh to sign deals with oil companies by Dec.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh to sign deals with oil companies by Dec.

text.p: Bangladesh on Thursday said it would sign exploration deals by December with international oil companies which were successful in the latest bidding round.
"We expect to finish evaluation (of the proposals) and reach contracts with successful bidders by December," Energy Minister Nooruddin Khan told a news conference in Dhaka.
"We want that the companies could start exploration work by next winter (January)," said the minister, flanked by senior officials and representatives of the bidders.

Some 20 multinational oil and gas companies and a state-run Bangladesh company participated in the bidding for exploration rights to explore 12 blocks in Bangladesh, nine of them onshore and three offshore. The government had offered 15 of the country's total 23 exploration blocks for bidding but three in northwestern region failed to attract bidders.
"We are very much encouraged by the response. All international big names are here. Their proposals indicate they are very serious," the minister said.

Officials said Cairn Energy Plc jointly with Shell Hydrocarbons Holdings BV, was the top bidder, seeking exploration rights in six blocks. Other major bidders included Chevron Corp, Enron Oil and Gas, Texaco Corp, Mobil Eastern E & D Inc, Unocal and Tullow Oil Plc. The Energy Ministry has appointed a U.S. consultancy firm, Arthur Anderson, to evaluate the proposals.
The government had earlier signed production sharing contracts with Occidental, Rexwood Oakland and United Meridian Co of U.S.A and Carin for eight blocks in east and southeast region.
Cairn has already struck gas in an offshore field while Occidental started drilling in June this year.
A fire at one of its rigs in northeastern Bangladesh forced Occidental to suspend drilling on June 15, but the company said it would soon resume exploration in the same filed.

Khan said the fresh exploration contracts would bring "billions of dollar" worth of investments to Bangladesh in next five years in exploration and production of gas and other "downstream businesses".
The state-run oil and gas corporation, Petrobangla, said it expected $100 million in investment in exploration in 1998 following signing of the agreements.

Cairn Energy and Occidental have already invested about $200 million. "It's a turning point for the economy of Bangladesh. Bangladesh is going to make its fortune out of the petroleum sector," Khan said.
Bangladesh has proven reserves of 10.2 trillion cubic feet (TCF) of natural gas.
The minister on Thursday said country's potential gas reserves were between 50 TCF and 80 TCF.
"If it comes out true, Bangladesh could be rated as a mid-level gas producing country," Energy Secretary Towfiq-e-Elahi Chowdhury told Reuters.
Representatives of foreign bidders said Bangladesh's potential gas reserves and liberal investment policy had lured them to take a stake here.
"We have no doubt that (gas) reserves are there. Regulatory changes in recent years are very much encouraging," said A.J. Penneycard, Project Manager of Shell EP International Ventures B.V.
"We see significant hydrocarbon potential in Bangladesh. My company is seeking a long term partnership," said Steven Hall, Vice President of Mobil eastern E and D Inc.
